semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the present-tense claim about venture focus and the surrounding investment framing.

contract.note: In this investment context, funding and sector reporting provide a fair ordinary reading of venture focus. The inferred period and funding measure affect the result. Funding does not directly measure enthusiasm.

evidence.note: Supports Part A: contemporaneous reporting identifies exceptional AI enthusiasm during H1 2023. It does not support the claim of little interest elsewhere.

AI received 18% of H1 funding, leaving about 82% outside AI. This contradicts Part B under the contract. The packet's explanation contains an arithmetic error: $10 billion is 40% of $25 billion, not over half.
July data shows AI received 11% of funding, while three other sectors each received more. This contradicts Part B and limits the evidence for sustained AI dominance.
Large non-AI rounds provide additional evidence against Part B. These examples alone do not establish the overall sector distribution.
The report was available before evaluation, but its full-year period extends beyond the statement. It cannot establish the funding distribution through August 10.

reviews.rationale: Part A holds under the contract's standout-sector reading: H1 reporting identifies strong AI enthusiasm. Part B fails: non-AI companies received about 82% of H1 funding, and three sectors each outdrew AI in July. The investment context makes this reading fair, although funding does not directly measure attention. The revenue-generating-company framing is not scored separately.
